What to look for in motorcycle jeans

  • Match your jacket. A 360° connection zip keeps your suit together in a crash — stick to one brand range where you can.
  • Knee and hip armour. CE Level 2 at the knees is the minimum; hip protectors matter in low-speed falls too.
  • Boot gaiters. Internal gaiters seal over your boots and stop rain running into your footwear.
  • Riding-position fit. Always try trousers seated — check the waist, knee articulation and length in your riding posture.

Frequently asked questions

How much should I spend on motorcycle jeans?

Our catalogue spans £132.99 to £300. Budget options under £150 cover the essentials, the £150–£400 mid-range hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers, and premium picks above £400 add refinement, lighter materials and longer-term durability.

Which brands are worth considering?

Popular, well-reviewed brands in this category include Klim, John, Trilobite, Spidi, Oxford, Merlin. All are stocked by SportsBikeShop with UK warranty support.

Textile or leather?

Textile is the practical all-weather choice for UK touring thanks to waterproof membranes and thermal liners. Leather offers the best abrasion resistance for spirited, dry-weather sport touring. Many riders own both.

faq.a: Quality riding jeans are far more than fashion. They use aramid fibres (the material behind Kevlar) either as a lining or woven single-layer construction, plus CE-certified knee armour and often hip protectors. Look for a CE garment rating: AA suits most road riding, while AAA jeans like the Trilobite Parado offer the highest abrasion resistance. Plain fashion denim offers almost no protection.

faq.q: What do AA and AAA ratings mean?
faq.a: Under the EN 17092 standard, riding garments are rated A, AA or AAA for abrasion, tear and seam strength, with AAA the highest. AAA jeans such as the Trilobite Parado are built for serious protection, sometimes in a single durable layer. AA jeans are a sensible balance of protection and comfort for everyday road riding. Always check the label rather than assuming.

Lined jeans stitch an aramid layer inside normal denim, which is affordable but can be warm and bulky. Single-layer jeans, like the Trilobite Parado AAA and John Doe options, weave the protective fibres into one fabric, so they are lighter, cooler and often achieve AAA ratings. Single-layer designs cost more but are more comfortable, especially in warm weather.

faq.q: Do riding jeans come with armour?
faq.a: Most quality riding jeans include CE-rated knee armour, and many have pockets for optional hip protectors that are sometimes sold separately. Check that the knee armour position is adjustable, because it must sit over your knee in a riding crouch, not when standing. If hip pockets are empty, adding CE hip inserts is a cheap, worthwhile upgrade.

Most riding jeans are not waterproof and will soak through in rain, though some treated denim resists light showers. For wet UK touring you are better served by dedicated waterproof textile trousers, or carry lightweight waterproof over-trousers to pull on. Jeans are best thought of as protective everyday wear for dry commutes and shorter rides.
